narrative: I opened a everyday checking account at the branch on the high street in March and was told in writing there would be no monthly maintenance fee if I kept a balance above a certain amount. My balance has never dropped below that amount, yet I have been charged a maintenance fee for four consecutive months. I called the contact centre twice and both agents agreed the fee was applied in error, but no refund has appeared. I am now being told the reversal request was never raised.

My savings account was frozen without notice while I was travelling. I could not withdraw cash or pay for my accommodation for six days. When I finally reached the fraud team they said a routine review had been triggered and that a letter had been posted to my old address, even though I updated my address on their app in January and have a confirmation email.

The bank applied three overdraft charges on the same day by reordering my transactions from largest to smallest. Had they posted them in the order they occurred, only one charge would have applied. I asked for an explanation of the posting order and was sent a generic leaflet that does not describe this practice at all.

I requested a closure of my current account in writing and received confirmation that the account was closed. Two months later a direct debit was allowed to draw on the closed account, taking it overdrawn, and I was then charged interest and a returned item fee on an account that was supposed to no longer exist.

I disputed a charge on my credit card for a gym membership I cancelled in person and in writing. The card issuer told me the dispute was resolved in the merchant's favour because the merchant supplied a signed contract, but the contract they supplied is the original joining form, not the cancellation. I have the cancellation receipt and have sent it three times.

My credit card interest rate was increased from a promotional rate to a much higher rate without the advance notice I believe I was entitled to. I have never made a late payment on this account. When I called to ask why, the representative could only tell me it was a periodic review and could not point me to anything I had done.

I was approved for a card with a stated credit limit, but the limit applied to the account was far lower. The higher limit appeared in the approval email and in the welcome pack. Customer service now says the approval email was an error and refuses to honour it or to remove the hard search from my file.

Someone made a series of small card-not-present purchases on my credit card over a weekend. I reported them the following Monday. The issuer reversed two of the charges but has left the remaining four on the account, saying they were within my usual spending pattern, which is not an explanation of why they consider them genuine.

I took out a personal instalment loan for a used vehicle. I have paid every month on time by automatic transfer, but the lender has applied several of my payments to a suspense account rather than to the loan, so the balance has barely moved. Nobody at the lender can explain what the suspense account is for or when the money will be applied.

I paid off my auto loan in full eight weeks ago and received a payoff confirmation letter. The lender has still not released the title and continues to show an outstanding balance in my online account. I cannot sell the vehicle without the title and the lender's title department does not answer its published phone number.

I asked my student loan servicer to place my loan into an income-driven repayment plan and submitted the income documentation twice. Both times the servicer said the documents were incomplete without saying which document or which field was the problem. Meanwhile the loan has gone delinquent and the delinquency is being reported.

The dealership arranged financing for me at one interest rate, then called a week later saying the finance company had declined and that I had to sign a new contract at a considerably higher rate or return the car. I had already been driving the vehicle for nine days and had traded in my old one, which they had already sold.

There is an account on my credit file that does not belong to me. I have filed a dispute with the credit reporting agency three times. Each time the dispute comes back verified as accurate within a few days, which cannot be a genuine investigation, and the agency will not tell me what the furnisher actually sent them to verify it.

A paid medical collection continues to appear on my report as unpaid. I have the receipt showing payment in full and a letter from the provider confirming the balance is zero. The credit reporting agency keeps closing my dispute as a duplicate even though the item has never been corrected.

My credit report shows a late payment for a month in which I was not late. The creditor has confirmed by phone that the reporting was a system error on their side, but they will not put that in writing, and the reporting agency will not remove the mark without something in writing from the creditor.

After I was a victim of identity theft I placed an extended fraud alert on my file and supplied the police report. One of the agencies continued to release my file to new credit applicants without contacting me, and two more fraudulent accounts were opened before I noticed.

A collection agency has been calling my workplace after I told them in writing that I cannot receive calls at work and asked that all contact be in writing. The calls have continued at a rate of several per week and my manager has now spoken to me about it. The agency denies receiving my letter, which I sent by recorded delivery.

I am being pursued for a debt that I do not recognise. I sent a written request for validation within the time allowed and have received nothing beyond a one-line statement showing a balance and an account number. Despite not validating the debt, the agency has continued to contact me and has now added fees.

A debt collector threatened to have me arrested and to contact my family members if I did not make a payment over the phone that day. When I asked for the agency's details in writing so I could check they were licensed, the caller hung up and has since called from a different number.

The collection agency is attempting to collect an amount considerably larger than the original balance, with no explanation of the additional charges. My original agreement does not permit collection fees of this size, and the agency has refused to send me a copy of the agreement they say allows them.

I sent an international wire through my bank to pay a contractor. The funds left my account and never arrived. The bank says the money was sent and the receiving institution says nothing arrived. Six weeks later neither side will open a trace and I have been told to take it up with the other party.

I used a peer-to-peer payment app to send money to a friend and mistyped one character of the handle. The money went to a stranger who has not returned it. The app told me that all transfers are final and that they cannot contact the recipient on my behalf, even though the transfer was flagged by their own system as unusual.

My prepaid money transfer card was declined at the point of sale even though it had a balance, and the balance was then unavailable for eleven days while a hold was investigated. I could not pay rent during that period. Nobody at the issuer could tell me who placed the hold or on what grounds.

I arranged a remittance to a family member abroad and was quoted an exchange rate and a fee at the counter. The amount actually received was materially lower than the quoted figure, and the receipt shows a different rate from the one on the board. The agent says the board rate is indicative only, which was not said at the time.

My mortgage was transferred to a new servicer and my escrow balance did not transfer with it. The new servicer says the escrow account is short and has raised my monthly payment substantially. The old servicer says the balance was forwarded. I have sent both a copy of my final escrow statement and neither will reconcile it with the other.

I applied for a loan modification and was told to stop making payments while the application was reviewed. The modification was then denied for non-payment, and the missed payments I was instructed to make are now being reported as delinquencies and have triggered a foreclosure referral.

The servicer paid my property taxes twice from my escrow account and then increased my monthly escrow payment to cover the resulting shortfall. The duplicate payment was refunded by the county to the servicer months ago, but my escrow analysis has not been redone and my payment has not come back down.

I asked for a payoff quote on my home loan and received one that includes a prepayment penalty. My original loan documents do not contain a prepayment penalty clause and the servicer cannot point to one. They have refused to issue a corrected payoff figure and my sale is now at risk.
